paper.title: Two-sided Competing Matching Recommendation Markets With Quota and Complementary Preferences Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Competing Matching under Complementary Preferences Recommendation problem (CMCPR)
unmapped: Two-sided many-to-one matching market run by a centralized platform: N firms (agents) and M types of workers (arms), K_m workers of type m
Firms have type-specific minimum quotas q_i^m and total quotas Q_i (complementary preferences)
Worker-to-firm preferences are known; firm-to-worker mean scores unknown and learned
Regret is firm-optimal stable regret relative to the firm-optimal stable matching, summed over firms and types (Bayesian social welfare gap)
Each matched firm-worker pair yields a noisy score (feedback for all matched pairs)
settings.definition_quote: If $p_i$ is matched with $a_j^m$ at time $t$, $p_i$ provides a noisy reward $y_{i,j}^m(t)$ which is assumed to be the true matching score $\mu_{i,j}^m$ plus a noise term ... sub-Gaussian ... Finally, define the Bayesian social welfare gap (BSWG) $\mathfrak{R}(T):= \mathbb{E}_{\theta \in \Theta}[\sum_{i=1}^{N}R_{i}(T,\theta)]$.

algorithms.name: Multi-agent Multi-type Thompson Sampling (MMTS) with double matching

symbols.Q: total quota of all firms, sum_i Q_i
symbols.K_max: maximum number of workers of a single type, max_m K_m
symbols.K: total number of workers, sum_m K_m

conditions: sub-Gaussian noise; mean scores in [0,1] implicitly used (confidence widths capped at 1)

source.label: thm: regret upper bound
source.quote: Assume $K_{\max} = \max\{K_{1},..., K_{M}\}, K = \sum_{m=1}^{M}K_{m}$, with probability $1-1/QT$, when all firms follow the $\mmts$ algorithm, firms together will suffer the Bayesian expected regret $$\mathfrak{R}(T) \leq 8Q\log(QT) \sqrt{K_{\max}T} + NK/Q.$$

results.notes: Statement mixes 'with probability 1-1/QT' and Bayesian expected regret; recorded as high-probability per the theorem text. Comparator is the firm-optimal stable matching (mapped to best_policy as closest). Theorem F.1 in the appendix restates the same bound (8 log(QT) sqrt(Q K_max) sqrt(QT) + NK/Q).

symbols.G_IC: sum over super-optimal workers l (negative super reward gap) of gap times min over covers of sum over blocking triplets of (C_{i,j,k'} + log(T)/d(mu_{j,u_min}, mu_{j,k'})), with C = O((log T)^{-1/3}); a negative O(log T) quantity

conditions: all firms other than p_i follow MMTS; firm p_i may deviate arbitrarily
Bernoulli KL d used, from Komiyama et al. TS analysis

source.label: thm: IC
source.quote: Suppose all firms other than firm $p_{i}$ follow the preferences according to the $\mmts$ to the centralized platform. Then the following upper bound on firm $p_{i}$'s optimal regret for $m$-type workers holds: $R_{i}^{m}(T,\theta) \geq \sum_{l: \overline{\Delta}_{i,l}^{m} < 0} \overline{\Delta}_{i,l}^{m}[...]$

results.notes: Incentive-compatibility result: lower bound on a single deviating firm's per-type regret (shows it cannot be more negative than O(log T)). Not a standard minimax/instance lower bound for all algorithms. Regret here is R_i^m(T, theta) for a fixed instance. Theorem G.1 restates it; Lemma 5.1/G.1/G.2 give the underlying pull-count bound.
